answer: Each identity must generate and retain a private memory-hard dataset, called a dune, from a yarrow seed bound to one signing key and committed on-ledger. In every short window the network issues a pulse query that is cheap to answer only if that exact dataset is kept hot. A yarrow seed reused across keys, two answers derived from one dune, or a missed window slashes the locked deposit. To operate N identities, an attacker generates, stores, and serves N distinct dunes from N yarrow seeds while funding N deposits, so memory, generation time, and capital all scale with farm size.
